newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends mixed after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends mixed after choppy session.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL

PALM OIL FUTURES - Prices finished mixed after choppy trade, with forecaster Ivan Wong's bearish data having impact on afternoon prices. Opening gains were due to soyoil's rises. Technically, the outlook remains bearish, and May futures is seen trading between 1,200 and 1,250 ringgit next week.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Lack of demand also saw cash prices slacken.
Wong had previously projected a fall of 21 percent.
Wong put end-February stocks at 670,000 tonnes and exports in February at 440,000 tonnes.

He said the speedy recovery in output was greatly assisted by good weather conditions in Peninsular Malaysia. "Technically, the market still looks weak despite rising initially on gains in soyoil last night," a chartist said, adding that technical selling also dragged down May futures to a low of 1,225 ringgit.
May futures contract managed to recover and closed unchanged at Thursday's 1,234 ringgit ($497.58) a tonne.
Among physicals, Mar (south) crude palm ol was offered at 1,282.50 ringgit against bids of 1,280 after trading from 1,280 to 1,275.
Mar (central) saw offers at 1,275 against bids of 1,270 with earlier trades done at 1,275 and 1270.
Apr (south) was offered at 1,277.50 with bids at 1,270, and Apr (central) at 1,265 with bids at 1,260.
Among refined products, Mar RBD palm oil was offered at $550 a tonne FOB Malaysia, Apr at $540 and May/June at $537.50. Mar was traded at $552.
Mar RBD palm olein saw offers at $580, Apr at $572.50 and May/Jun at $565. Mar was dealt at $582, $581 and $577.50.
Mar RBD palm stearin was offered at $455 and Mar/Apr palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $310.
